ticker.label: BLIZZCON 2026 SIGNAL
ticker.text: STARCRAFT returns as an open-world shooter • Diablo V enters a fallen Sanctuary • World of Warcraft: Forever launches November 4 • Forsaken Kingdom is live and under review

upserts.title: STARCRAFT
upserts.issue: A return to the Koprulu Sector as an open-world shooter must preserve StarCraft’s military science-fiction identity, faction conflict, tactical competence, danger, scale, and hard-edged war atmosphere rather than using the name for a generic open world.
upserts.audienceSignal: Blizzard used the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony to reveal STARCRAFT as an original open-world shooter targeting Spring 2030. The return of the franchise and major genre shift create the event’s strongest new Watch case, but a cinematic announcement is not proof of the finished game.
upserts.shortRuling: Top to Watch. StarCraft’s return is a major audience event; judge whether the open-world shooter preserves the Koprulu Sector’s warfare, factions, competence, danger, and identity.

upserts.title: Diablo V
upserts.issue: Diablo V must preserve Sanctuary’s brutal dark-fantasy identity, demonic horror, meaningful class power, danger, consequence, loot progression, and the struggle against overwhelming evil.
upserts.audienceSignal: Blizzard officially announced Diablo V for Spring 2029 with Sanctuary fallen, its heroes defeated, and Diablo victorious. The premise is unusually dark and franchise-forward, but the game remains years away and its systems, monetization, classes, and finished execution are unresolved.
upserts.shortRuling: Top to Watch. The fallen-Sanctuary premise fits Diablo’s core darkness; judge the actual classes, progression, danger, monetization, and finished campaign rather than the announcement alone.

upserts.title: World of Warcraft: Forever
upserts.issue: A permanent Vanilla-era branch must respect Warcraft’s original world, faction identity, community, exploration, class roles, danger, progression, and social adventure without turning nostalgia into a cosmetic storefront.
upserts.audienceSignal: Blizzard announced Forever as a third World of Warcraft experience alongside Modern and Classic, with three new zones, more than 1,000 quests, nine dungeons, two raids, and the Skyborne race. Beta begins September 17 and global launch is November 4, 2026; optional paid upgrade bundles and the reimagined-era premise require scrutiny.
upserts.shortRuling: Top to Watch. A world-first, community-first Vanilla branch could restore core Warcraft strengths, but launch quality, progression, class identity, monetization, and long-term stewardship must earn the verdict.

upserts.title: Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom
upserts.issue: The first new Warcraft III campaign in more than two decades must honor Lordaeron, the Forsaken, Sylvanas, strategy-game identity, established lore, and the consequences connecting Warcraft III to World of Warcraft.
upserts.audienceSignal: Blizzard released the Forsaken Kingdom campaign during BlizzCon 2026 with a prologue, three story chapters, a neutral Forsaken Paladin hero unit, new story content, the 3.0 graphics update, and a revamped World Editor. Availability is confirmed, but finished-player reception and campaign durability are not yet established.
upserts.shortRuling: Unranked Watch. A real new Warcraft III campaign is significant, but its lore fidelity, strategic depth, technical execution, and audience response require finished review before any final ruling.
